To: t-4471
Replying to: p04
Cc: none
Subject: Official response and November 14 clinic update

Cascade Legal Rights Project appreciates the opportunity to respond. We understand why people are concerned. Receiving a lawyer’s letter soon after asking for help is frightening, especially when you are already worried about your home. We take those concerns seriously, and we will not discuss any individual’s situation publicly.

Our clinic policy prohibits landlords and their attorneys from receiving attendee information and prohibits the sharing, sale, or disclosure of that information. Sign-in records are retained internally in locked storage.

Magistrate-court eviction filings are public records, and some law firms use those filings to send mailings to tenants. These public filings are the likely explanation for the letters described here.

We also want neighbors to know that the free tenant-rights clinic is still happening this Saturday, November 14, from 10 a.m. to 1 p.m. Because the East Atlanta Library meeting room will be closed for HVAC repairs, the clinic has moved to the Mt. Zion Fellowship Hall. The side entrance by the parking lot is accessible. No appointment is needed.

Volunteer attorneys and staff can review eviction notices and court papers and explain your options. You are still welcome, whether you have questions about a notice, court papers, or where to turn next.

If you attended a clinic and have concerns about your information, please contact us directly so we can address them without discussing your circumstances in public. Questions or concerns can be sent to clinic@cascaderights.example, or you can call our office at 404-555-0187. Thank you to the moderator for inviting us to respond.
